properties.name: A what-if on a principle assumed in an argument's steps shows which positions hold only under it, which still hold by another line, and which objections come back
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-10-20 ("go with your recommendations on the 3 choices from earlier", choice 2: assumed principles, with the what-if fixed in phase 6)
properties.statement: When an argument takes a principle as an assumption in the steps that apply it (the design-an-argument recipe), a what-if on dropping that principle reads every position that rests on it: which lose all support (they held only under it), which still hold by another line (naming that line's assumptions), and which objections it answered come back. Today a what-if on an assumed principle says nothing about the positions. MEASURED 2026-10-20 on the trolley design (phase 6 PR 1, #779): dropping act consequentialism should leave the footbridge "push" verdict unsupported and the bystander "turn" verdict standing on double effect (the observer's fall-out, worked by hand).
